item.title: Self-Hosted C++ Networking Libraries: Asio vs libhv vs POCO for High-Performance Services
item.description:
Introduction

When building self-hosted network services in C++, choosing the right networking library shapes everything from throughput to code complexity. Whether you’re writing a custom reverse proxy, a game server backend, or a REST API handler, the networking layer determines how efficiently your service handles concurrent connections, manages I/O, and scales across CPU cores.

item.title: C++ WebSocket Libraries: WebSocket++ vs Boost.Beast vs IXWebSocket vs libwebsockets vs wslay (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Real-time communication is the backbone of modern distributed systems — chat applications, live dashboards, financial tickers, multiplayer game servers, and collaborative editing tools all depend on persistent bidirectional connections. For C++ developers building high-performance backends, choosing the right WebSocket library has direct consequences on throughput, latency, memory usage, and integration with existing async frameworks.
